name: Royal
lede: Royal is a dark, vivid blue-violet from the ISCC-NBS dictionary of color names, and a far darker, more saturated color than the familiar web color Royal Blue despite the shared word.

sections.title: Not the same blue as its namesake
sections.body:
ISCC-NBS block 146 places it as a dark green in the 1955 dictionary, 7.1 units from the hex #0C1793, a loose match, and Maerz and Paul's earlier 1930 catalog is cited as a source without a specific plate recorded here [1]. No Munsell notation survives for it in our library, unusual among its neighbors [1].

Despite the name, it sits roughly 34 units away in Lab space from [[royal-blue|Royal Blue]] (#4169E1), the much lighter, more familiar web and Crayola color, and about the same distance from [[royal-purple|Royal Purple]] [1]. Its closer library neighbor is plain [[dark-blue|Dark Blue]] (#00008B), 8.0 units off, still a visibly different, more neutral blue, with [[zaffre|Zaffre]] and [[egyptian-blue|Egyptian Blue]] both a little further out again [1]. The word "royal" has long attached to deep, costly-looking blues and purples without settling on one exact mix, and this dictionary entry is one of several competing claims to the name [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of it covers at least five percent of the canvas in just 1 of our 23,781 archive paintings, as photographed, rarer than 82 percent of our named colors [2]. In that single painting it plays an accent role rather than a shadow or a light [2]. The sample is too small here for a reliable first-seen date or century pattern, which is itself a finding: this exact mix is close to absent from our painting record [2].
